assessment.summary: KRAS is a well-validated, highly druggable oncology target with exceptional structural coverage (556 PDB entries, best resolution 0.953Å), two FDA-approved covalent inhibitors (sotorasib and adagrasib targeting G12C), and over 5,900 ChEMBL IC50 entries. Despite historical reputation as 'undruggable,' the field has clearly demonstrated tractability, though the median IC50 of ~1 µM reflects the ongoing challenge of achieving potent engagement across diverse KRAS mutants beyond G12C. Literature support is among the strongest of any cancer target with >8,000 publications and active 2026 research.
evidence_gaps: Approved drugs (sotorasib, adagrasib) are specific to KRAS G12C mutation; druggability of other clinically relevant mutants (G12D, G12V, G12R, Q61H) remains less established with fewer approved agents
Median IC50 of ~1020 nM across ChEMBL entries suggests many chemical series lack high potency, indicating the broader chemical space is not yet well optimised
Resistance mechanisms (e.g., acquired G12C→G13D, bypass signalling via RTKs, SHP2 pathway) limit clinical durability and are not fully resolved
Pan-KRAS inhibitors and KRAS wild-type selectivity windows are still under active investigation with no approved agents
KRAS G12D and G12V inhibitor clinical data are still early-stage; no approved drugs for these predominant pancreatic and colorectal mutants
Allele-specific vs. non-selective inhibitor strategies for combination regimens not yet fully clinically validated
